Mythology.question: Who is the Greek god of the sea?
Mythology.fun_fact: He was also the god of earthquakes and horses.

Mythology.question: Who is the wife of Zeus and the queen of the gods?
Mythology.fun_fact: The Romans called her Juno, and the month of June is named after her.

Mythology.question: How was the goddess Athena born?
Mythology.fun_fact: She had no mother. Hephaestus split Zeus's head open with an axe to let her out.

Mythology.question: What gift did Athena give the city of Athens?
Mythology.fun_fact: Poseidon offered a salt-water spring, but the city chose Athena's gift and named itself after her.

Mythology.question: Who stole fire from the gods to give it to humanity?
Mythology.fun_fact: As punishment, an eagle ate his liver every day, and it grew back every night.

Mythology.question: Which Titan was punished by Zeus by having to hold up the heavens on his shoulders for eternity?
Mythology.fun_fact: The Atlantic Ocean and books of maps are both named after him.

Mythology.question: Which god of wine, parties and theatre was "born twice", the second time from Zeus's thigh?
Mythology.fun_fact: The Romans called him Bacchus, which is where the word "bacchanal" (a wild party) comes from.

Mythology.question: Who was the first woman in Greek mythology, created by the gods and given a jar she was told never to open?
Mythology.fun_fact: Her name means "all-gifted".

Mythology.question: What was the only thing left inside Pandora's jar after all the evils of the world escaped?
Mythology.fun_fact: In the original myth it was a jar. The "box" comes from a 16th-century mistranslation.

Mythology.question: Who is Odysseus's wife, famous for her patience and cunning?
Mythology.fun_fact: She kept her suitors away for 20 years by weaving a shroud by day and secretly unravelling it every night.

Mythology.question: Which king was punished in Tartarus by rolling a boulder uphill for eternity?
Mythology.fun_fact: His crime was cheating death, twice.

Mythology.question: What mythical creature has the head of a bull and the body of a man?
Mythology.fun_fact: It lived in the Labyrinth on Crete until the hero Theseus killed it.

Mythology.question: What is the name of the one-eyed giant in Greek mythology?
Mythology.fun_fact: Odysseus escaped the Cyclops Polyphemus by blinding him and telling him his name was "Nobody".

Mythology.question: Which Greek monster, with snakes for hair and a gaze that turns people to stone, was born a mortal woman before the goddess Athena cursed her?
Mythology.fun_fact: The hero Perseus beheaded her, using a polished shield as a mirror.

Mythology.question: What many-headed Greek beast grew back two heads for every head that was cut off?
Mythology.fun_fact: Heracles defeated it by having his nephew burn each neck stump.

Mythology.question: Which monster, with a lion's body and a human head, killed anyone who couldn't solve her riddle about the stages of human life?
Mythology.fun_fact: Oedipus solved the riddle, and the answer was "a human": crawling as a baby, walking as an adult, and using a cane in old age.

Mythology.question: In Roman myth, what were the names of the twin brothers who were rescued by a she-wolf and went on to found Rome?
Mythology.fun_fact: Romulus killed Remus in an argument, and the city was named after him.

Mythology.question: What is the Roman equivalent of Zeus?
Mythology.fun_fact: The largest planet in the solar system is named after him.

Mythology.question: Which Roman god of war was the father of Romulus and Remus, and gave his name to both a month and a planet?
Mythology.fun_fact: March was originally the first month of the Roman year, because it was when military campaigns began.

Mythology.question: Which jackal-headed Egyptian god watched over mummification and the dead?
Mythology.fun_fact: Priests sometimes wore Anubis masks while mummifying the dead.

Mythology.question: He is the king of the underworld and the judge of the dead, always shown as a mummified king with green skin, a symbol of rebirth and agriculture. Who is he?
Mythology.fun_fact: He was murdered by his jealous brother Set, and his wife Isis brought him back to life.

Mythology.question: In the Egyptian "weighing of the heart", what was the dead person's heart weighed against?
Mythology.fun_fact: A heart heavier than the feather was eaten by the monster Ammit.

Mythology.question: Why does Thor's hammer Mjölnir have an unusually short handle?
Mythology.answer: Loki, disguised as a fly, bit the dwarf forging it
Mythology.fun_fact: Loki had bet his own head that the dwarves couldn't make better treasures than his favourite smiths.

Mythology.question: Which Slavic witch lives in a hut that stands on chicken legs?
Mythology.fun_fact: She flies around in a large mortar and steers with a pestle.

Mythology.question: Which Slavic goddess of spring and youth, known from Slovenian folklore, has a name that is an old Slavic word for spring?
Mythology.fun_fact: Her opposite is Morana, the goddess of winter. In Poland she's called Marzanna, and people still drown a straw figure of her every spring to chase winter away.

Flags of the World.question: Which country's flag is this?
